heroSub: The Story of Fankaar Institute of Performing Arts, Jaipur.
story: Fankaar began with a simple conviction: that Indian classical arts are not museum pieces but living practices, and anyone with a zeal to learn deserves a guru who takes their journey seriously. What started as a handful of Kathak students in Jaipur has grown into an institute of four branches and an online classroom, having trained more than 175 students, including three CCRT scholarship awardees.

The name itself reflects the mission. Fankaar (फनकार), meaning “artist,” represents our belief that every learner has an artist within them waiting to be nurtured. From a six-year-old taking their first steps in Tatkaar to an adult preparing for an Alankar, every class is designed to awaken that artist through a meaningful and disciplined learning journey. At Fankaar, we train for depth, not display—with a focus on strong technique, a living repertoire, and the discipline that creates space for genuine creative freedom.
mission: Fankaar exists to preserve the purity and timelessness of India’s classical and folk performing arts. Through dedicated mentorship and disciplined training, we guide every student towards creative freedom, awakening the Fankaar—the artist within.

founder.name: Vartika Tiwari
founder.role: Leading Kathak Dancer & Founder of Fankaar Arts
founder.bio: Vartika Tiwari is a distinguished Indian classical dancer, choreographer, and Kathak exponent based in Jaipur, Rajasthan. With over 20 years of dedicated training in Kathak, she has developed a deep understanding of the Jaipur Gharana tradition. Her artistic journey began under the guidance of Pt. Girdhari Maharaj of the Jaipur Gharana and was further refined under the mentorship of eminent Guru Ishira Parikh. Rooted in the Guru-Shishya tradition, her practice brings together intricate footwork, rhythmic precision, dynamic movement, and expressive storytelling. Vartika holds a Master of Performing Arts (Kathak) from Gujarat University, along with classical dance diplomas from Bhatkhande Sangeet Vidyapeeth, Lucknow; Akhil Bhartiya Gandharva Mahavidyalaya Mandal, Mumbai; and Rajasthan Sangeet Sansthan, Jaipur. In 2018, she was awarded the CCRT Scholarship by the Centre for Cultural Resources and Training (CCRT), Ministry of Culture, Government of India, in recognition of her dedication to Indian classical dance. In 2021, she founded Fankaar Arts with four students, with a vision to create a space where Indian classical arts could be learned through authentic training, mentorship, and discipline. Today, Fankaar Arts has grown into a vibrant learning community with four branches across Jaipur—Malviya Nagar, Tonk Road, Jagatpura, and Nirman Nagar—alongside its online classroom, nurturing learners of different age groups in Kathak and Hindustani music while encouraging them to develop both technical excellence and a deeper artistic connection with tradition.

approach.title: Guru–Shishya Parampara
approach.text: Small batches, close mentorship, and personal attention. Every student is observed, guided, corrected, and encouraged with care, reflecting the depth and personal connection of the traditional Guru–Shishya approach to learning.

approach.title: A Structured Path
approach.text: Training follows a structured progression through recognised examination levels, from foundational stages to advanced certifications, with opportunities to appear for examinations conducted by established institutions including Bhatkhande Sangeet Vidyapeeth, Lucknow; Akhil Bharatiya Gandharva Mahavidyalaya Mandal, Mumbai; and Pracheen Kala Kendra, Chandigarh.

approach.title: The Stage as Classroom
approach.text: Recitals, showcases and community performances are an integral part of the curriculum. Students learn to carry their art into the world with confidence, grace and poise.
